title: Avoiding repetition
goal: Refer back to people and ideas without repeating the same words, using pronouns, ce dernier and celui-ci, summary nouns and synonyms.

items.fr: le, lui, en, y / ce dernier / celui-ci

drills.text: La bibliothèque est neuve. Les familles ___ fréquentent beaucoup.
drills.en: The library is new. Families go there a lot.
drills.explain: [[fréquenter quelque chose]] takes a direct object: [[la bibliothèque]] → [[la]].

drills.text: Karim a parlé à Olivier. ___ dernier lui a donné de bons conseils.
drills.en: Karim spoke to Olivier. The latter gave him good advice.
drills.explain: [[ce dernier]] = the last person mentioned (Olivier), masculine singular.

drills.text: J'ai rencontré Lucie et sa sœur. ___ habite à Moncton.
drills.en: I met Lucie and her sister. The latter (the sister) lives in Moncton.
drills.explain: The last person mentioned is feminine: [[cette dernière]] or [[celle-ci]]. [[Elle]] would be unclear: Lucie or her sister?

drills.prompt: Which verb can replace “a” in « La ville a trois piscines » in a formal text?
drills.explain: [[compter]] = to have, to number: [[La ville compte trois piscines.]] It sounds more written than [[avoir]] or [[il y a]].

items.en: the latter (the last person or thing mentioned)

example.fr: J'ai écrit au propriétaire, mais ce dernier n'a pas répondu.
example.en: I wrote to the landlord, but the latter didn't answer.

items.en: this one, she (for a feminine noun just mentioned)

example.fr: Amira a appelé la directrice, mais celle-ci était en réunion.
example.en: Amira called the principal, but she was in a meeting.

example.fr: Ce phénomène touche toutes les grandes villes.
example.en: This trend affects all the big cities.

example.fr: La population est invitée à donner son avis.
example.en: The public is invited to give its opinion.

example.fr: Trouver un logement est un vrai défi.
example.en: Finding housing is a real challenge.

example.fr: Le maire souligne l'importance du projet.
example.en: The mayor emphasizes the importance of the project.

example.fr: Elle affirme que le service est gratuit.
example.en: She states that the service is free.

items.en: to have (available), to be equipped with

example.en: The school has a large gym.

items.en: to carry out, to make (a formal action)

example.fr: La ville a effectué des travaux cet été.
example.en: The city carried out work this summer.

steps.title: Same text, less repetition
steps.intro: Karim writes a short article for his neighbourhood newsletter in Laval. Read his first draft. Count how many times you see **la bibliothèque** and **les gens**.

blocks.title: First draft
blocks.fr: Depuis septembre, notre quartier a une nouvelle bibliothèque. La bibliothèque a une salle pour les enfants et la bibliothèque a aussi des ordinateurs. Les gens aiment beaucoup la bibliothèque. Les gens vont à la bibliothèque le soir et les gens vont à la bibliothèque la fin de semaine. La directrice, madame Gagnon, dit que la bibliothèque a déjà 3 000 abonnés. Madame Gagnon dit aussi qu'il y a un problème : il y a peu de places de stationnement. Le problème est sérieux.
blocks.en: Since September, our neighbourhood has a new library. The library has a children's room and the library also has computers. People really like the library. People go to the library in the evening and people go to the library on weekends. The director, Ms. Gagnon, says that the library already has 3,000 members. Ms. Gagnon also says that there is a problem: there are few parking spaces. The problem is serious.

blocks.title: Revised version
blocks.context: The same information, with pronouns, ce dernier, summary nouns and synonyms.
blocks.fr: Depuis septembre, notre quartier dispose d'une nouvelle bibliothèque. Celle-ci compte une salle pour les enfants ainsi qu'une vingtaine d'ordinateurs. Les habitants l'apprécient beaucoup : ils y vont le soir comme la fin de semaine. Selon la directrice, madame Gagnon, l'établissement a déjà 3 000 abonnés. Cette dernière souligne cependant une difficulté : il existe très peu de places de stationnement. Ce problème, de l'avis de nombreux usagers, est sérieux.
blocks.en: Since September, our neighbourhood has had a new library. It has a children's room as well as about twenty computers. Residents appreciate it a lot: they go there in the evening as well as on weekends. According to the director, Ms. Gagnon, the facility already has 3,000 members. She points out a difficulty, however: there are very few parking spaces. This problem, in the opinion of many users, is serious.

blocks.prompt: In the revised version, what does “Celle-ci” refer to?
blocks.explain: [[Celle-ci]] refers to the **last feminine noun** mentioned: [[une nouvelle bibliothèque]].

blocks.prompt: In “ils y vont”, what does y replace?
blocks.explain: Review (A2): [[y]] replaces a place introduced by [[à]]: [[ils vont à la bibliothèque]] → [[ils y vont]].

blocks.prompt: Why does Karim write “Cette dernière” and not “Elle”?
options: Elle could mean the library or the director; cette dernière clearly means the director
blocks.explain: Two feminine nouns are in play ([[la bibliothèque]], [[la directrice]]). [[Cette dernière]] points to the **last one mentioned**, so there is no confusion.

blocks.title: Tool 1: pronouns you already know
blocks.body:
Use the pronouns from A2 to replace a noun you've just mentioned:

- **direct object** → [[le, la, l', les]]: [[Les habitants apprécient la bibliothèque.]] → [[Ils l'apprécient.]]
- **indirect object (à + person)** → [[lui, leur]]: [[J'ai écrit à la directrice.]] → [[Je lui ai écrit.]]
- **a place, or à + thing** → [[y]]: [[Ils vont à la bibliothèque.]] → [[Ils y vont.]]
- **de + thing, or a quantity** → [[en]]: [[Elle a 3 000 abonnés.]] → [[Elle en a 3 000.]]

Remember the position: the pronoun goes **before the verb**, or before the auxiliary in the passé composé: [[Je l'ai lu.]]

blocks.title: Tool 2: ce dernier and celui-ci
head: masculine
feminine
blocks.note: Both point to the **last noun mentioned**, and agree with it. Use them when [[il]] or [[elle]] would be ambiguous: [[Olivier a appelé Karim. Ce dernier était malade.]] (= Karim). [[Ce dernier]] is very common in news and formal writing; [[celui-ci]] is a little more neutral. Don't overuse them: once or twice per text is enough.

blocks.title: Tool 3: summary nouns
blocks.note: Sum up a whole idea with a general noun: [[cette situation]], [[ce problème]], [[cette décision]], [[ce phénomène]], [[cette mesure]] (this measure), [[ce projet]]. It links your sentences and shows the reader you are still on the same topic.

examples.fr: Les loyers ont augmenté de 20 % en trois ans. Ce phénomène touche surtout les jeunes familles.
examples.en: Rents have gone up 20% in three years. This trend mainly affects young families.

examples.fr: La ville a fermé deux piscines. Cette décision a surpris les habitants.
examples.en: The city closed two pools. This decision surprised residents.

blocks.title: Tool 4: synonyms for overused words
head: Instead of…
try…
Example
rows: il existe, on trouve, on compte
Le maire souligne l'importance du projet.
La ville a effectué des travaux.
les habitants, la population, les citoyens, les usagers
La population est invitée à donner son avis.
une difficulté, un défi, un obstacle
Trouver un logement est un vrai défi.
blocks.note: A synonym must keep the **same meaning** and the **same grammar**: [[disposer de]] needs [[de]]; [[affirmer que]] + a full sentence. [[un usager]] is a user of a public service (transit, library).

blocks.title: Repetition traps
blocks.body:
- **Ce dernier for the wrong noun:** it always means the **last** noun mentioned. In [[Karim a parlé à Olivier. Ce dernier…]], ce dernier is Olivier, not Karim.
- **No agreement:** [[la directrice… ce dernier]] is wrong → [[cette dernière]]. [[celui-ci]] for a feminine noun is wrong → [[celle-ci]].
- **Celui alone:** [[celui]] needs [[-ci]], [[-là]], [[qui]], [[que]] or [[de]] after it. Never write *Celui est grand.*
- **The dictionary trap:** not every synonym fits. [[posséder]] (to own) works for a person or a company, not for a library's opening hours. When in doubt, keep the simple word.
- **Disposer without de:** [[La salle dispose d'un écran]], not *dispose un écran*.
- **Changing the pronoun:** if you start with [[on]], continue with [[on]], not [[nous]] then [[vous]].

blocks.title: Why does French dislike repetition more than English?
blocks.body:
English tolerates repeating a key word (*the library… the library…*) for clarity. French school writing, on the other hand, treats repetition as a **style error**: teachers circle it in red. In exams like the TEF and TCF, using pronouns and varied vocabulary is part of the **lexical range** and **cohesion** criteria.

The trick is balance: repeating a key word once is fine; repeating it five times in a paragraph is not.

blocks.title: A few Canadian words in Karim's article
blocks.body:
- [[la fin de semaine]] = the weekend in Québec ([[le week-end]] in France).
- [[un abonné]] = a library member or a subscriber. In Québec, a library card is [[une carte d'abonné]] or [[une carte de bibliothèque]].
- [[le stationnement]] = parking, and also a parking lot in Québec ([[un parking]] in France).

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: In [[ce dernier]], the e of [[ce]] is often barely heard: *s'dernier*. In [[celle-ci]], you hear *sel-si*.

blocks.fr: Sofia a présenté son projet à monsieur Roy. Ce dernier l'a trouvé excellent.
blocks.en: Sofia presented her project to Mr. Roy. He found it excellent.
blocks.explain: [[Ce dernier]] = the last person mentioned, [[monsieur Roy]]. And [[l']] replaces [[son projet]].

blocks.fr: Le service d'autobus a été réduit le dimanche. Cette décision inquiète beaucoup les usagers.
blocks.en: Bus service has been reduced on Sundays. This decision worries users a lot.
blocks.explain: A summary noun ([[cette décision]]) sums up the whole previous sentence.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Each sentence repeats something. Find the best way to avoid it.

blocks.text: J'ai acheté le livre et je ___ ai lu en deux jours.
blocks.en: I bought the book and I read it in two days.
blocks.explain: Direct object [[le livre]] → [[le]], which becomes [[l']] before [[ai]]. The pronoun goes before the auxiliary.

blocks.text: Raj a rencontré Mei et son mari. ___ travaille dans une banque.
blocks.en: Raj met Mei and her husband. The latter (the husband) works in a bank.
blocks.explain: The last noun is [[son mari]]: masculine singular → [[ce dernier]] or [[celui-ci]].

blocks.prompt: « Les loyers augmentent depuis cinq ans. ___ touche surtout les étudiants. » Which summary noun fits best?
blocks.explain: [[Ce phénomène]] sums up the whole idea: rents rising for five years.

blocks.prompt: Match each everyday word with a more formal synonym.
There are several solutions. (formal, without “il y a”)
blocks.explain: [[Il existe]] + noun is the formal equivalent of [[il y a]]. Like [[il y a]], it stays singular: never *ils existent* here.

blocks.en: The room has a big screen.
blocks.explain: [[disposer de]] = to have, to be equipped with. Don't forget [[de]] (here [[d']]).

blocks.text: Mes voisins vont souvent au parc. Ils ___ vont le dimanche.
blocks.en: My neighbours often go to the park. They go there on Sundays.

accept: Cette décision a surpris les habitants
blocks.explain: A summary noun ([[cette décision]]) + a synonym for *les gens* ([[les habitants]]).

blocks.prompt: I wrote to the landlord, but the latter didn't answer.
accept: J'ai écrit au propriétaire, mais ce dernier n'a pas répondu.
J'ai écrit au propriétaire, mais celui-ci n'a pas répondu.
J'ai écrit au propriétaire mais ce dernier n'a pas répondu.
J'ai écrit au propriétaire mais celui-ci n'a pas répondu.
blocks.explain: [[écrire à]] → [[au propriétaire]]; then [[ce dernier]] for the landlord. Review (A2 unit 7): writing to a landlord!

blocks.fr: Cette dernière souligne une difficulté importante.

blocks.prompt:
Rewrite this repetitive paragraph so that it reads well. Keep all the information. Then add one or two sentences of your own about a public place you like (a library, a park, a community centre).

« Dans ma ville, il y a un nouveau parc. Le parc a une piscine et le parc a des jeux pour les enfants. Les gens adorent le parc. Les gens vont au parc tous les jours. Le maire dit que le parc a coûté deux millions de dollars. Le maire dit aussi que le parc va avoir une patinoire l'hiver. »
checklist: At least two pronouns (le / la / l' / y / en / lui)
celui-ci / celle-ci or ce dernier / cette dernière, with the right agreement
A summary noun: ce projet, cette décision…
Two synonyms: il existe, disposer de, souligner, les habitants…
The key word (le parc) appears no more than twice

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Ma ville dispose d'un nouveau parc. Celui-ci compte une piscine ainsi que des jeux pour les enfants. Les habitants l'adorent : ils y vont tous les jours. Le maire affirme que ce projet a coûté deux millions de dollars. Il précise aussi qu'on y installera une patinoire l'hiver. Moi, j'aime surtout la bibliothèque de mon quartier, car elle organise des ateliers de conversation. J'y vais tous les samedis.
models.en: My town has a new park. It has a pool as well as play equipment for children. Residents love it: they go there every day. The mayor states that this project cost two million dollars. He also specifies that a skating rink will be installed there in winter. Personally, I especially like the library in my neighbourhood, because it organizes conversation workshops. I go there every Saturday.

summary:
- Replace nouns with the pronouns you know: [[le, la, les, lui, leur, y, en]]
- Point to the last noun mentioned with [[ce dernier / cette dernière]] or [[celui-ci / celle-ci]], with the right agreement
- Sum up an idea with [[ce phénomène, cette décision, ce problème]], and vary common words: [[il existe, disposer de, souligner, les habitants]]
